findings.title: Second downsize definition overrides width/height API
findings.body: Ruby keeps only the later `self.downsize` (line 149). The method defined at line 145, which builds a `#{max_width}x#{max_height}` geometry, is never callable. Existing callers that pass numeric width and height now hit the dimensions form, so the height integer is treated as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises NoMethodError, and even if that is avoided the geometry is a bare width with the height dropped. Thumbnail/downsize jobs that still use the old signature will fail or resize incorrectly.

findings.title: ImageMagick convert reads and writes the same tempfile
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is invoked with the upload tempfile path as both source and destination. `convert` opens the output before it finishes reading the input, so an in-place resize commonly truncates or corrupts the file (often to an empty or partial image). The upload is then stored from that same path via `Upload.create_for`, so users can lose the original and end up with a broken image instead of a downsized one. Downsize must write to a separate temp path and replace the upload file only after success.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and 80% geometry is wrong
findings.body: The loop never checks the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize`. On failure the same file is retried until `attempt` hits 0, then `Upload.create_for` still runs. The geometry passed is `"80%"`, and `downsize_instructions` always appends `\>` (shrink-only), producing `-resize 80%\>`. ImageMagick does not treat that as a valid percentage shrink, so convert typically exits non-zero and the image is never reduced below `max_image_size_kb`. Oversized uploads therefore still fail, or a partially written file is saved.

findings.title: Client size check ignores site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` used to compare against `SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and images are no longer limited by `max_image_size_kb`. If an admin set a limit below 10MB, the composer accepts files the server will reject; if the image limit is above 10MB, legitimate uploads are blocked client-side and the automatic downsize path never runs. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoded 10MB, so the alert text does not match the real limit.

findings.title: URL downloads always capped at 10MB for every type
findings.body: `FileHelper.download` previously used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` and now always passes `10.megabytes`, before the code knows whether the URL is an image. Non-image API uploads ignore `max_attachment_size_kb` (larger attachments that the site allows are truncated/rejected at 10MB; smaller limits are not enforced here). Image URLs bigger than 10MB never reach the new downsize loop, so the feature does not cover the large remote images it is meant to shrink, and the cap cannot be configured.
